newsitem.title: FRANCE: Canal Plus, TF1 step up satellite TV row.
newsitem.headline: Canal Plus, TF1 step up satellite TV row.

text.p: French pay TV firm Canal Plus has stepped up its campaign to be able to carry French public television channels on its satellite station, commissioning a poll that backs its stand.
Canal Plus and private French channel TF1 have been locked in a battle over their rival digital satellite TV offerings.
Canal Plus has been campaigning to get French public channels France 2 and France 3 on Canalsatellite, its satellite television unit.

At the moment public channels are carried on rival Television Par Satellite (TPS), the satellite station controlled by private channel M6-Metropole TV and its parents in which TF1 has a 25 percent stake.
Satellite subscribers can receive terrestrial television channels, but not in digital quality or with the possibilities that digital television offers.

Some 84 percent of the 1,000 people surveyed in the poll, to appear in weekly Tele Sept Jours on Monday, said it was wrong to have to subscribe to a satellite station to receive public channels. The poll, by polling institute IFOP for Canalsatellite, was made available by Tele Sept Jours on Friday.
TPS, however, says if Canal Plus used the decoder developed by TPS shareholder France Telecom, Canalsatellite subscribers could receive the public channels in digital form.

"Today, talks with Canal Plus, which has become used to being the sole actor in the pay television market, are not simple," TPS managing director Cyrille du Peloux said in an interview with Tele Sept Jours.
"TPS has always been in favour of developing a common terminal which would give access to public channels, but also, for example, to first division football matches broadcast by Canal Plus," he said.
But Canal Satellite managing director Bruno Delecourt told the magazine the station's subscribers felt they were being discriminated against.

"They are nearly 300,000 homes and will be over half a million at the end of the year, and there is a feeling of discrimination. It is as if motorways were reserved for a single make of car," Delecourt said.
He added, however, that CanalSatellite was now implementing the single terminal solution using simulcrypt software, which can read any digital television broadcast.

Canal Plus has also been waging its campaign against TF1 in front of Parliament, which is currently discussing a broadcasting bill that will give the new digital satellite television stations a legal framework.

On Thursday, Canal Plus vice chairman Marc-Andre Feffer attacked TF1 at a parliamentary committee, saying the absence of France 2 and France 3 from Canalsatellite was prejudicial, "skews free competition" and amounted to discrimination between private operators by the public sector.

"We do not understand that Canalsatellite subscribers, who pay the TV licence fee, cannot receive France 2 and France 3 while TPS subscribers, who also pay their licence fee, can receive them," he told the committee examining the bill.
